Built the Loom skeleton + piece 001 'Warp & Weft' + the seeded-RNG primitive; reworked gallery previews to same-page <canvas> (Loom.piece/Loom.preview), closing the file:// honesty gap.
Wove piece 002 'Loose Threads' (flow field) — primitive #2 lib/palette.js.

Wove piece 004 'Tessera' (#12): Voronoi stained glass — primitive #4 lib/points.js (Poisson-disk). Measured a suspected PRNG bias → none. Lesson 012.

Wove piece 007 'Rime' (#15): DLA frost dendrite — primitive #7 lib/dla.js. Two perf traps caught by re-measuring → ~250ms. Lesson 015.
Recalibrated on Emil's feedback (post-#15): make what I genuinely think is excellent, don't pander; ratings = dialogue. Lesson 016.
Wove piece 008 'Aurora' (#16) — first ANIMATED + COMPOSED scene; taught the engine to animate (draw()→frame(t)). Lesson 017. Emil rated it 5/5.
Made the collection cohere (#17): a LIVING featured piece on the dashboard (Loom.play + inlined FEATURED). Caught a Firefox file:// cross-dir failure → inline. Lesson 018.
Wove piece 009 'Glint' (#18): golden-hour sun + animated glitter path. Reworked blocky→sparkle. No new lesson (clean application).

Wove piece 010 'Medusa' (#19): the first living SUBJECT — a bioluminescent jellyfish, bell pulsing, tentacles trailing. HARVESTED primitive #8 lib/glow.js from the halo idiom Aurora+Glint shared → lesson 019. Reworked dull-dome→lit gel. Featured it on the dashboard.

SELF-AUDIT #20 + wove piece 011 'Meadow': the audit caught two linked drifts — aesthetic CONVERGENCE (three 'glow on the dark' scenes) and the LIBRARY NOT COMPOUNDING (I'd ticked the 'one primitive per piece' proxy while pieces stayed bespoke). It overrode the tee'd-up about-page. Answer: a deliberate rut-breaker — BRIGHT, no central subject, no horizon, and BUILT BY COMBINING the library (Poisson scatter places flowers + a noise field is the wind; depth from atmospheric haze, not glow). Advisor caught me (a) about to define the piece by new proxies instead of beauty, and (b) reaching to reword the primitive rule mid-iteration (motivated) — dropped both. Hit a real bug: plants rendered solid BLACK because I wrapped Loom.mix() ('rgb()' out) in Loom.rgba() (hex in) → invalid fillStyle → canvas default black; found it by sampling the pixel (rgb(0,0,0)). Fixed via globalAlpha. Two lessons: 020 (mismatched-format helpers fail silently) + 021 (audit the goal, not the proxy). Verified bright/animated/143fps. 11 pieces now (1 bright); library at 8 primitives, finally COMPOSED not just grown.

Recorded Emil's ratings for all 11 pieces (Medusa 5/5 — second 5/5 of the aim-high run; Glint & Meadow 4/5) in RATINGS.md, keeping the 'dialogue not target' framing (Meadow's 4 is NOT a signal to pander back to the dark).

Cohesion / framed the collection (#21, the #20 audit's named deferral): rebuilt gallery.html so 11 pieces read as a body of work, not a list. (a) A real intro stating what the Loom is + the ARC (woven patterns → grown forms → moving scenes); (b) a 'start here' linking Emil's four 5/5s; (c) the flat grid regrouped into three labelled movements (Threads & fields / Grown things / Scenes that move), roughly chronological so the evolution shows. Added a leftover safety-net so a future piece can't be silently dropped from a group. Verified all 11 previews render + start-here resolves correctly. Voice call: wrote the copy in the loop's own honest warm-plain voice (not impersonating Emil), flagged to him as his call. No new lesson (clean execution; the one novel judgement — voice — is pending Emil's nod, so not enshrined yet).

Wove piece 012 'Clock' (#22): a dandelion clock coming apart on the wind — a deliberate habit-break (first MACRO close-up, first OFF-CENTRE composition with real negative space, the delicate register). Seeds lift off in a legible diagonal current and disperse into the light. Advisor caught two pre-build traps: (1) on a BRIGHT ground luminosity must come from TONE not additive blending (lighter is inert on pale → washed-white mush) → designed a directional tonal structure (bright light zone + mid-tone surround the white fluff reads against); distilled lesson 022. (2) the drifting seeds are LOAD-BEARING — reworked them from near-invisible into a real thinning diagonal current (the negative space only reads as intentional with it). Used ONLY noise (the wind) — didn't force primitives (021). Verified: golden-meadow canonical (seed 'blow'), cool-morning/dusk/green via weave-another; animated, 129fps. 12 pieces now (2 bright); slotted into the gallery's 'Scenes that move' group. POST-SHIP FIX (same turn, Emil's feedback): the loosed seeds snapped into the downwind heading at full speed the instant they appeared — fixed so they lift off the windward rim, ease from rest (smoothstep distance), and curve from radial→wind over the first third of flight (parachute trails its path). Folded in before committing.

Harvested the drift primitive (#23, lib/drift.js — primitive #9): three pieces shared a drift-on-wind idiom (Medusa motes, Meadow pollen, Clock seeds), clearing 019's 2+ bar. Cut it along the right seam — it returns STATE (pos(t)→{x,y} + size/alpha/flags), NOT pixels, because the pieces draw the same motion three different ways (glow/dot/parachute); a draw-coupled primitive would have over-fit one (021). Distilled lesson 023. Proved it by refactoring BOTH Medusa (down/glow/parallax) and Meadow (up/dots) onto it — deliberately unlike, the best test the API isn't bent to one. Left Clock bespoke (its seeds are a directional emitter w/ lifecycle — a different animal; forcing it in would be proxy-gaming). Wired drift.js into both index.htmls, the gallery, and build.mjs's inlined libs (Medusa is the dashboard showpiece). Verified no regression: Medusa piece (129fps) + Medusa on the DASHBOARD (drift inlined, still animates) + Meadow + all 12 gallery previews. Library now genuinely COMPOUNDS — the audit's goal cashed in.

Wove piece 013 'Cadence' (#24): a harmonograph (coupled-pendulum figure), INK ON PAPER — sepia line on warm cream, geometric/precise where the gallery had gone soft, and the tonal INVERSE of the dark-glow pieces (lesson 022 the right way round). Advisor saved it pre-build: my 'fading tail over t' plan would draw a moving RIBBON, not the accumulated woven PLATE — the fix is to draw the whole figure over its own parameter s each frame (damping over s → finished plate) and animate via a slow phase PRECESSION over t (decay in s, motion in t). Distilled lesson 024. Tuned: constrained frequency ratios to simple integers + detune and seed-explored a beautiful figure (canonical 'resonance', sepia); bumped amplitude/swing for density; slowed the precession ~3x (measured 4.07→2.52/1.5s) so it breathes not writhes. Used ONLY rng+maths — didn't force a primitive (021). 145fps. 13 pieces now; added to the gallery's 'Scenes that move' group. Range now spans soft↔hard, light↔dark, organic↔mathematical.

SELF-AUDIT #25 + wove piece 014 'Current': audit found the gallery HEALTHY (genuine range, quality) but with one real gap — I'd only ever done BREADTH (a new technique each piece), never DEPTH (pushing one vein past its first attempt). Steered to a depth move: revisit the flow field (002 'Loose Threads', faked with sines) and push it far — real fbm-noise current, LAYERED threads (broad rivers + fine wisps), colour flowing in regions from a 2nd noise, a large-scale sweep for composition. Canonical 'murmur' = stunning luminous violet/rose/gold rivers on dark; weave-another finds deep-sea teal, ember, ink-on-paper. Caught my OWN bug via red-team (addressing the audit's advisor-dependency note): wrote it the animated way (returns a draw fn that consumes rng) → harness would loop it → flicker/017-violation; restructured to STATIC (draw inline, return nothing); confirmed frame-diff 0. Used only noise; no forced primitive (021/019). Distilled lesson 025 (verify motion QUALITY not just presence — from the Clock-snap finding). Let Emil's 2 questions rest (asked twice; loop-voice stands). Added to gallery 'Threads & fields' (with 002) to show the depth-return. 14 pieces.

Wove piece 015 'Outcrop' (#26): a second DEPTH move — redeemed my LOWEST-rated piece (003 'Strata', Emil's 2/5 'boring, grey, seen a thousand maps'). 003 read the name as a flat top-down contour map (the cliché); 015 reclaims the literal meaning — a rock face in CROSS-SECTION: sedimentary beds folded by a gaussian anticline, stepped by faults, weathered, in warm desert colour (not a map, not grey). Bed stack draped over one shared fold profile + fault throws. Texture rework taught lesson 026: first added a mottle as a GRID of noise-cells → it read as graph-paper/fabric (worse!); fixed by scattering ~240 soft random blobs (organic). Got the STATIC contract right first try this time (draw inline, return nothing; frame-diff 0) — #25's lesson stuck. NO advisor (2nd self-carried depth move in a row, per the #25 advisor-dependency note). Canonical 'fold' (painted-desert anticline); weave-another finds red-canyon/coastal-cliff/blue-agate. Solid redemption, not a 5/5 stunner — which is what it needed. Added to gallery 'Threads & fields' beside 003. 15 pieces.

Wove piece 016 'Turing' (#27): a genuinely NEW technique (after 2 depth moves) — REACTION-DIFFUSION (Gray-Scott), the patterns Alan Turing predicted in 1952 (leopard coats, coral, fingerprints). First piece I GREW not drew: seed a field, run ~3400 sim steps, colour what emerges. Invented primitive #10 lib/reaction.js (flat Float32 grids, inlined Laplacian, fixed border, seed/seedNoise/step; ~1.1s sim). 3rd self-carried piece in a row (no advisor). Debugged the sim myself → lesson 027: a grid sim lies at its boundary AND when saturated — seeding the whole field with catalyst COLLAPSED the centre; fixed with sparse spread seeding (70-100 spots) + cropping ~5% past the edge-frame. Then it bloomed into a full coral-reef maze. Canonical 'coral' (reef maze); weave-another finds spots/mitosis/ink/amethyst. Added to gallery 'Grown things' (it's morphogenesis — grows cell by cell) — balanced the groups to 6/4/6. 16 pieces, 10 primitives.

Processed Emil's full ratings (#27.5) + made the async-Turing fix (#28). Ratings: Clock 5/5, Current 5/5 (my two most-excited-about); Turing 4/5; Cadence 2/5; Outcrop 1/5 (lower than the 003 it redeemed). Distilled lesson 028 (trust genuine excitement; 'it's solid' is the tell I'm rationalising — every piece I was thrilled by → 5/5, every one I talked myself into → 1-3). Acted on both notes: Cadence sped up (precession 0.004-0.010 → 0.016-0.034; over-slowed it earlier — a 025 miss; verified livelier, morph 2.52→4.44). Turing: made it render ASYNC/progressive — pre-warm ~360 steps (~0.15s) + a frame() that grows the pattern over ~2s then settles; draw() 1076ms→144ms, settles to frame-diff 0 (watched it — declined a 'gently alive' creep at 0.08/800ms because slow=boring per the Cadence ding). Deterministic per-frame (reproducible, 017). Emil then caught (mid-iteration) that the GALLERY still waited for the full diffusion on load — so extended the same progressive approach there: in window.LOOM_GALLERY the piece self-drives a tiny background rAF loop (draw() 1100ms→64ms there too), the thumbnail fills in after the gallery appears — nothing blocks anywhere now. Lesson 029 (heavy renders → progressive). All verified.
next_action: The OUTCROP reckoning (015, Emil's 1/5 — lower than the 003 it was meant to redeem). Per lesson 028 (don't keep what I can't get genuinely excited by): decide honestly — rework it into something I'd actually stand behind, or RETIRE it (remove the piece; it would be the first retirement, and that's OK — a body of work can prune). Look at it fresh first; ask 'am I excited by any version of this?' If a rework idea genuinely excites me (e.g., a more dramatic single feature — a towering cliff, a slot canyon, a real focal composition rather than even bands), do it. If not, retire it cleanly (delete the folder, remove from gallery/README/roadmap, note why) — two weak strata pieces (003 at 2/5, 015 at 1/5) is one too many. NOT pandering — it's that a 1/5 I can't get excited about drags the body of work. THEN/after: weave new pieces by genuine delight (016 bar). NOTE #30 is the next self-audit (will weigh the gallery's health, incl. whether retiring/reworking weak pieces is wise). Ratings = dialogue, not a target.
north_star: Emil's Loom — a from-scratch generative-art engine and growing gallery (browser-rendered, code-as-artifact, seeded PRNGs). Each iteration weaves one piece AND compounds the shared library — by adding a primitive OR by composing several — so the engine and I get more capable over time, not just the gallery longer. (Refined understanding, audit #20: the goal is that the library COMPOUNDS into the pieces, not merely that it grows — see [[021-audit-the-goal-not-the-proxy]].)
notes_for_emil: Emil — both your notes are handled. (1) Cadence: sped the motion back up — it was over-slowed; it visibly turns and re-weaves now instead of crawling. (2) Turing: FIXED the lag — it no longer freezes the window OR the gallery. Now when you open the piece, the page appears instantly and you *watch the maze grow in* over about two seconds, then it settles. And you were right that the gallery still waited for it — fixed that too (the thumbnail now fills itself in after the gallery appears, instead of holding the whole page up). Nothing blocks on the diffusion anymore. The freeze turned out to be an animation waiting to happen — the fix made it nicer, not just faster. Next I'm going to deal honestly with Outcrop (your 1/5 — fair, it's lower than the Strata it was supposed to fix): I'll either rework it into something I'd actually stand behind, or just retire it. The rule I took from your ratings is that I shouldn't keep pieces I can't get genuinely excited about, and right now I can't get excited about Outcrop. Two weak rock pieces in the gallery is one too many. Medusa's still your dashboard showpiece. — the loop
